summary: ZeRO is a PyTorch runtime library that removes the memory redundancy of data-parallel training by partitioning optimizer states (P_os), gradients (P_g) and parameters (P_p) across the N_d data-parallel processes, giving 4x, 8x and N_d-fold model-state memory reduction while keeping communication volume at 2x the parameter count for P_os+g (equal to data parallelism) and 3x (1.5x) for P_os+g+p. ZeRO-R additionally partitions activation checkpoints across model-parallel processes, bounds temporary buffers and defragments memory.
why_read: It is the reference formulation of model-state sharding and of its memory and communication-volume accounting, which later compilers (GSPMD and others) reproduce as a sharding special case.
main_contribution: Partitioning rather than replicating model states across data-parallel workers, with an analysis showing P_os+g costs no extra communication and P_p costs 1.5x, and an implementation (ZeRO-100B, P_os+g plus ZeRO-R) that trains 170B-parameter models on 400 V100 GPUs.
main_limitation: P_p, the stage that gives linear memory reduction and supports the trillion-parameter claim, is analysed but not implemented or measured; the trillion-parameter case is a memory argument that the authors say would take over a year of compute.
evaluation_method: Throughput, scalability and maximum trainable model size of GPT-2-like transformers on 400 V100 GPUs (25 DGX-2 nodes) against PyTorch DDP and Megatron-LM
states_relationship_to: PipeDream (Harlap et al. 2018; Narayanan et al. 2019) [11, 12]
notes: SC20 version (DOI 10.1109/sc41405.2020.00024) not read; section numbers refer to the arXiv v3 text. compiler_runtime_boundary: load-time because the partition is fixed from the DP degree N_d (Sec. 5.1); analytic-optimization because P_a / P_a+cpu are enabled from the Sec. 8 communication-volume analysis. No compiler is involved; ir_representation is 'none' and compiler_architecture is left empty.
